02 — Butcombe

Byre conversion

The work

The byre had stood open on one side for forty years and the roof was the only part worth keeping. We propped it, took the walls back to sound stone, and rebuilt underneath.

The owners wanted to keep the cattle stalls visible in the hallway, so the ground floor is laid out around them. Underfloor heating, lime plaster, and a steel frame you can't see holding the middle of the roof up.

Location
Butcombe
Scope
Full conversion, 190 m²
Duration
11 months

Steve Chiverton

I've been building in and around Wrington for over twenty years. Most of our work comes from direct recommendation; by people who have seen our work locally, or from families we've already worked for over the years.

I have been a builder from the moment I could climb a ladder, worked as a qualified plumber for 14 years. I still run every site myself, if you ring the number on this website, you get me. Our entire team is dedicated to building your dreams.

Every project is different – that's all part of the fun – and after many years in the business, we've learned there are ways and means to produce high quality results at every aspect of even the most complex builds.

What Master Builder registration means

The Federation of Master Builders inspects finished work and checks the accounts before it lets anyone join, and again periodically after. It is not a badge you buy. It also means there is somewhere independent to complain to, which matters more than it sounds.

How it goes

From the first phone call to the day we hand the keys back. Nothing here is a stage in a diagram; it is what actually happens.

01
You ring
Ten minutes on the phone. I'll tell you straight away if it isn't the sort of job we do, or if we're booked past the point that's useful to you.
02
I come and look
An hour at the house, usually within a fortnight. No charge, no obligation, and I won't bring anyone to sell you anything.
03
A rough figure
A range, in writing, within a week — enough to know whether to carry on. It is a range because at this stage anything narrower would be a guess dressed up.
04
Drawings and permissions
If you don't have an architect I'll suggest two or three who work near here. Planning and building control take as long as they take; I'll tell you what's realistic.
05
The proper quote
Itemised, with a start date and a finish date, and a written note of what would change the price. Payment falls in stages against work done, never in advance.
06
On site
Same faces every day. Start at eight, off site by five, swept up on Fridays. One short update from me each week, whether or not there's anything to report.
07
Snagging and handover
We walk round together and you write the list. It gets done before the final payment, not after. Then a two-year warranty, and you can still ring me in five.
